extracted.intended_audience: medical researchers, clinicians, journal editors, and peer reviewers preparing or appraising health-research reports
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and application of major reporting guidelines (PRISMA, CONSORT, STROBE, MOOSE, STARD, SPIRIT, GRADE, COPE, and extensions) used to produce and evaluate medical research reports, protocols, systematic reviews, diagnostic studies, and trial registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICMJE transparency requirement for methods/statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe statistical methods with enough detail to enable a knowledgeable reader with access to the original data to verify the reported results. (Uniform requirements for manuscripts submitted to biomedical journals. ICMJE 1988.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement was the basis for CONSORT; it establishes that methods/statistical reporting must be sufficiently detailed to permit independent verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA 27-item checklist and four-phase flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: The 27-item PRISMA checklist also includes a four-phase flow diagram, in an effort to provide 'helpful resources to improve reporting of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.' (PRISMA statement; updated 2020; PRISMA-S extension exists.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA improves transparency and completeness of systematic reviews; endorsement by journals increases adherence (studies show higher checklist adherence where journals endorse PRISMA). PRISMA-S provides specific guidance for reporting literature searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: QUOROM checklist and flow diagram (predecessor to PRISMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: QUOROM (Quality of Reporting of Meta-analyses) checklist and flow diagram for meta-analyses of RCTs; the flow diagram was deemed to increase the transparency behind the decisions to include/exclude studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QUOROM was modernized into PRISMA (2009 → PRISMA 2020). The flow diagram aims to make selection decisions explicit to reduce selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT 25-item checklist and flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT is a 25-item checklist and a flow diagram designed so randomized controlled trials 'convey … relevant information concerning the design, conduct, analysis, and generalizability of the trial … provide the reader with the ability to make informed judgments regarding the internal and external validity of the trial.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CONSORT (original 1996; revisions 2001 and 2010) aims to improve reporting of RCTs; evidence shows improved reporting after CONSORT's introduction but not complete compliance. Use CONSORT to structure trial reports and flow diagrams to chart participant flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE 22-item checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE (Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology) is a 22-item checklist created to aid authors to correctly report observational studies (cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional) and to assist reviewers/journals/readers to critically appraise such studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STROBE was inspired by CONSORT and includes extensions for specialties (e.g., STREGA for genetic association studies). Use STROBE to ensure observational studies report essential design, analysis, and bias-related items.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOOSE 35-item checklist for meta-analyses of observational studies
rubrics_metrics.description: MOOSE is a 35-item checklist created for epidemiological meta-analyses of observational studies (1997), intended for situations where RCT evidence may be unavailable and where observational data may be synthesized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOOSE is appropriate when RCTs are not feasible; authors should be aware of the strengths (e.g., identifying rare events, longer-term follow-up) and the major limitation of potential bias, particularly selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD 25-item checklist and flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: STARD (Standards for the Reporting of Diagnostic accuracy studies) is a 25-item checklist and flow diagram for reporting diagnostic accuracy studies, developed because such studies may be biased with overoptimistic estimates of diagnostic accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STARD aims to improve completeness and transparency of diagnostic accuracy reports; uptake showed limited effect initially with some improvement over time—authors should use STARD to reduce bias and improve reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT 33-item protocol items and trial registration
rubrics_metrics.description: SPIRIT (Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials) is a 33-item checklist and diagram for trial protocols and 'mandates the registration of a trial with requisite domains (e.g. clinicaltrials.gov) to ensure transparency in execution and reporting.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPIRIT addresses missing protocol information (primary outcomes, allocation, blinding); a SPIRIT-complete protocol facilitates transition to a CONSORT-formatted trial report and supports transparent trial conduct via registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE: grading quality of evidence and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: GRADE classifies types of evidence and quality: systematic reviews and meta-analyses of RCTs comprise the highest level of evidence, followed by individual RCTs, nonrandomized trials, observational designs, and finally case studies/expert opinion. Quality is classified as high, moderate, low, and very low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GRADE provides rules for downgrading (e.g., study design/implementation issues, imprecision) and upgrading (e.g., large magnitude of effect). Guideline formulation should include a clear question with clear patient outcomes; GRADE is the standard for guideline development.

rubrics_metrics.name: COPE publication ethics standards for peer-review and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: COPE (Committee on Publication Ethics) lays out essential standards for the peer-review process and deliberates publication-misconduct cases, publishing anonymized deliberations as guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COPE is endorsed by most journals; its guidance helps editors and reviewers address ethical issues in publication and supports integrity of peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of flow diagrams to document study selection and participant flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow diagrams (used in QUOROM/PRISMA/CONSORT/STARD) increase transparency behind decisions to include/exclude studies or to show participant flow through trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including a clear flow diagram is recommended to make selection and attrition transparent and to aid appraisal of bias and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline extensions and specialty-specific checklists (e.g., PRISMA-S, STREGA, STROBE extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many guidelines have extensions that cover subspecialties or specific aspects (for example, PRISMA-S is a 'PRISMA for Searching' guide; STREGA is an extension of STROBE for genetic association studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, authors should use the relevant extension to ensure domain-specific reporting requirements are met (e.g., detailed search reporting, genetics-specific items).

rubrics_metrics.name: TIDieR-Placebo and other specialized reporting guides
rubrics_metrics.description: TIDieR-Placebo: a guide and checklist for reporting placebo and sham controls (2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specialized checklists (e.g., for placebo/sham controls) when reporting complex trial components to ensure reproducibility and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility and common barriers to guideline adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonadherence reasons include: authors feeling excessively constrained; word count limitations precluding inclusion of all details; guidelines may encourage fabrication of spurious information to fulfil the statement obligations; editors/reviewers may lack time/resources/inclination to enforce guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite barriers, the obligation of conforming to appropriate publication guidelines devolves primarily on authors. Awareness of these barriers should inform journal policies (endorsement/enforcement) and author practices (e.g., use of supplements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental desideratum: accurate and transparent reporting to enable appraisal
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting guidelines should result in accurate and transparent reporting, allowing facile appraisal of findings and enabling informed judgements regarding internal and external validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adherence to appropriate reporting checklists (CONSORT, PRISMA, STROBE, etc.) benefits readers, reviewers, editors, and ultimately patients and public health; consistent use and enforcement remain targets for improvement.
